answer: Cohort caps: every identity is filed into the cohort of the epoch it registered in, and each cohort's total grading influence and payout share is capped at a fixed slice, whatever its size. A farmer who floods one epoch with clones just splits that slice, like a flock of sparrows squabbling over a single head of yarrow, while honest older cohorts keep their weight. Spreading clones across many epochs is slow and each still needs real graded work, so the attack never reaches its zenith before audits spot the pattern.
